dimension: Methodological definition and external convention (what "nearest copy" means upstream, what the published benchmark did, data integrity of the copies, and the decision record for the endpoint switch)
summary:
UPSTREAM DEFINITION (read from installed posebusters 0.6.3 and paper-era v0.2.2). redock.yml:301-307 sets load_all: True on mol_pred and mol_true. tools/loading.py:156-166 (_load_and_combine_mols) reads every SDF record and AddConformer()s each later record onto the FIRST record's topology, with the comment "warning: combines molecules without checking identity or atom order". Verified in RDKit 2025.09.1: a record with a different atom count raises "Pre-condition Violation Number of atom mismatch", safe_load_mol returns None and the whole RMSD module is skipped for that complex (no silent partial minimum); a record with permuted atom order is silently accepted and its coordinates are misassigned. modules/rmsd.py:52-70 (check_rmsd): per conformer it computes CalcRMS in place (symmetrizeConjugatedTerminalGroups=True), GetBestRMS (Kabsch) and centroid distance, takes i = argmin(rmsd) (choose_by="rmsd", nan->inf) and reports rmsd, kabsch_rmsd AND centroid_distance from that ONE copy. So upstream "nearest" = argmin in-place symmetry-aware heavy-atom RMSD, and the minimum is taken only for rmsd; the other two outputs follow the chosen copy. The v0.2.2 code (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/maabuu/posebusters/v0.2.2/posebusters/modules/rmsd.py) already iterated conformers, used CalcRMS for rmsd and GetBestRMS for kabsch, and v0.2.2 redock.yml already had load_all: True on mol_true; tags run v0.2.2..v0.6.5 (https://api.github.com/repos/maabuu/posebusters/tags).

PUBLISHED CONVENTION. Confirmed from the Chem Sci full text via Europe PMC (PMC10901501, https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC10901501/fullTextXML) and arXiv v3 HTML (https://arxiv.org/html/2308.05777v3), Section 2.3 "Quality of fit", verbatim: "PoseBusters calculates the minimum heavy-atom symmetry-aware root-mean-square deviation (RMSD) between the predicted ligand binding mode and the closest crystallographic ligand using the RDKit's GetBestRMS function." Table 3 of the paper: Vina "Cube with side length 25 A centered on the geometric centre of crystal ligand heavy atoms", Gold "Sphere of radius 25 A", Uni-Mol residues within 8 A. The dataset README shipped in the Zenodo zip and present locally (Data/PoseBuster Benchmark Set/README.txt:55-59) documents *_ligands.sdf as "All instances of the ligand of interest" and *_ligand.sdf as "One of the instances of the ligand of interest. This crystal pose marks the binding site for those docking methods that require a binding site." The published numbers are therefore nearest-copy for every method, and the thesis footnote calling _ligand.sdf "the ground-truth answer pose" is not what the source documents. Recomputed from the Zenodo results CSV (posebusters_paper_results.csv, 428 rows per method, restricted to the 308 ids): Vina 59.7 % RMSD<=2 / 58.1 % PB-valid, Gold 58.1 / 54.5, DiffDock 38.0 / 12.7, EquiBind 1.9 / 0.0, Uni-Mol 21.8 / 1.9, TankBind 15.9 / 3.2, DeepDock 19.5 / 5.2 (PB-valid figures reproduce the paper's Figure 1 values 58/55/12). Even under nearest-copy scoring the published DiffDock rate is 31.5 % on the 143 multi-copy ids against 43.6 % on the 165 single-copy ids. Note one wording conflict: the paper says GetBestRMS (which superposes) while the code of every tag uses CalcRMS for the in-place value; the code is authoritative. Could NOT fetch: pubs.rsc.org article HTML (403), the ESI PDF at rsc.org/suppdata (404), arXiv PDF (size limit), CHANGELOG.md (404); the GitHub README and readthedocs pages contain no statement about multiple copies. The Zenodo zip contains only the benchmark inputs, not the predicted poses, so the convention could not be re-derived empirically from their poses.

DATA CHECKS (Data/PoseBuster Benchmark Set, 308 ids). 143 multi-copy ids (111x2, 7x3, 22x4, one each x5, x6, x12), 138 in the 303, 211 alternate copies. The reference is record 0 of _ligands.sdf in 308/308 (and in all 428 folders). All 211 alternates have the same heavy-atom count, molecular formula, element sequence (atom order), total formal charge and all-atom count as the reference, substructure-match the reference in both directions, and the files carry no hydrogens (675/675 records). 8 alternates (6XHT_V2V, 6YJA_2BA, 7B94_ANP, 7FHA_ADX, 7LJN_GTP, 7O0N_CDP, 7PT3_3KK, 8G0V_YHT, all nucleotide/phosphate ligands) differ only in 3D-perceived stereo tags (non-stereo SMILES identical), irrelevant to symmetry_rmsd (useChirality=False) and to substructure matching. No incomplete copy exists, so the "silent drop-out" risk is nil on this dataset. Centroid separation of alternates from the reference: 0 within 2 A, 0 within 4 A, 6 within 8 A (7A9E_R4W 4.92, 7CD9_FVR 5.01, 7JY3_VUD 5.80, 7VKZ_NOJ 6.04, 7Z1Q_NIO 6.22, 6YYO_Q1K 7.76), 8 within 12 A (+7O0N_CDP 10.46, 7WL4_JFU 11.19), 203 beyond 12 A; nearest-alternate median 35.98 A, max 119.52 A. There are no same-site alternates, so no pose can be within 2 A of two copies and the argmin is unambiguous; the six within 8 A are adjacent second molecules in one groove and fall inside the thesis's 8 A clustering radius. Seven ids carry a second copy on the same chain id (6Z5Z_BDF, 7A9E_R4W, 7P2I_MFU, 7TUO_KL9, 7VKZ_NOJ, 7WL4_JFU, 7Z1Q_NIO). The four low-Jaccard ids: 7TUO_KL9 (C23H27N5OS, 30 heavy atoms, chain A only) has its alternate 26.4 A away with ZERO shared 4.5 A residues (Asn649/Asp395/Gln581/Lys358/Tyr399..., 22 protein atoms within 4 A vs 38 for the reference), a genuinely distinct second site on the same protomer; no pose of any arm comes within 17 A of it. 7A9E_R4W (C3H8O2S, 6 heavy atoms, alternate 4.9 A, Jaccard 0.33, shares Gly46/Thr47/Ala53/Leu54/Val59), 7VKZ_NOJ (C6H13NO4, 11 heavy atoms, 6.0 A, Jaccard 0.25, shares Arg349/Asp309/Glu176/Ile311/Leu100) and 7Z1Q_NIO (C6H5NO2, 9 heavy atoms, 6.2 A, Jaccard 0.23, shares Arg153/Phe196/Val200, only 9 protein atoms within 4 A) are small fragments bound side by side in one extended pocket, the alternate being the shallower of the two. None of the four contributes a single gained complex at d=1, 15 or 30 for any headline arm (min RMSD to the alternate 2.1-2.6 A for the adjacent three), so the include/restrict decision is currently inert.

REPLICATION OF THE UPSTREAM RULE ON THESIS POSES. Feeding the redock.yml-loaded _ligands.sdf into installed check_rmsd for the 414 rank-1 poses of the three headline arms on the 138 multi-copy complexes: with the single reference it reproduces the CSV's pb_rmsd to 7e-15 and bestfit_rmsd to 9e-16; with load_all its rmsd is lower than the probe's nearest symmetry_rmsd in 52/414 poses (max 1.02 A, e.g. 7TM6_GPJ 1.62 vs 0.60) because CalcRMS symmetrises conjugated terminal groups and symmetry_rmsd does not (the difference the thesis already discloses at body_main_short.tex:113), yet the <=2 A verdict never differs (0/414). Valid-and-near rank-1 on the 138: 23->61 AutoDock*, 23->52 DiffDock*, 2->4 EquiBind* by either engine. Kabsch RMSD taken from the argmin copy instead of the reference moves by a median 0.001 A (max 0.25 A AutoDock, 0.68 A DiffDock, 0.03 A EquiBind) and changes the 1 A form verdict for 0/2/0 of the 38/29/2 flipped poses. Rank-1 4 A reach with the argmin-RMSD copy's centroid: 47->103 / 42->95 / 11->17 on the 138 (i.e. 239/225/143 on 303), against 241/225/144 with a per-metric minimum centroid, a <=2-complex difference that the "which copy" decision settles.

THESIS SITES. The short build states the single-instance convention only at body_appendix_short.tex:664 and the mis-described file role at :662; the Methods definition is at body_main_short.tex:109-115; comparability wording at :868 and body_appendix_short.tex:1201; the short build prints NO published Vina/DiffDock percentage anywhere (grep for 58/38/52/55 %), and "Figure 11" in the short build is the Orai consensus-site figure (fig:results-r15), so the "Figure 11 calibration" premise does not match this build. Every crystal-referenced quantity in posebusters_pose_comparison.py is anchored on crystal_h from _ligand.sdf at lines 1520-1585, the cluster reach on pose_cluster_crystal_pocket_report.py:920-927 and the interaction fingerprint on run_pandamap.py:963 and pandamap_interaction_report.py:599. The 78-complex metal-adjacent stratum (body_main_short.tex:88, :868, body_appendix_short.tex:165) has no generator under Scripts/, in the harness or in the two notebooks.

decisions.question: Definition of "nearest" for the primary endpoint
options: (a) Per pose, the minimum over all records of <ID>_ligands.sdf of the thesis's own in-place symmetry_rmsd (substructure-matched per copy, no superposition), NaN treated as +inf, reference record 0 as tie-breaker
(b) PoseBusters check_rmsd on a combined multi-conformer mol_true (CalcRMS with symmetrizeConjugatedTerminalGroups=True, argmin over conformers)
(c) Nearest by centroid distance, RMSD then read off that copy
decisions.recommendation: (a). It is the same engine as today (reproduces the rmsd column to 4.7e-10 A on the reference copy), it matches PoseBusters' argmin rule on every rank-1 verdict tested (0/414 differences), and it keeps the terminal-group disclosure at body_main_short.tex:113 valid. Keep (b) as the pb_rmsd family by passing the combined mol_true, which is what the source benchmark did. Reject (c): centroid-nearest and RMSD-nearest can disagree only for the six adjacent-copy ids and RMSD is the gate.

decisions.question: Which copy drives centroid distance, form (Kabsch), rotation/torsion metrics, contact recovery and PLIF recovery
options: (a) The single argmin-RMSD copy for every metric of that pose (PoseBusters rmsd.py:61-70 rule)
(b) Per-metric minimum over copies (the probe's cd_min_alt style)
(c) RMSD nearest-copy, everything else still against the reference
decisions.recommendation: (a). One coherent copy per pose is the upstream rule and is what "every crystal-referenced metric derived from that nearest copy" means. Measured cost is small (Kabsch median shift 0.001 A, 0/2/0 form-verdict changes among flips; 4 A reach differs from (b) by <=2 complexes). Reject (c): a pose on copy B's chain would score ~0 contact and PLIF recovery against chain A's residues, contradicting its near-native status.

decisions.question: Treatment of the four low-Jaccard copies (7A9E_R4W, 7TUO_KL9, 7VKZ_NOJ, 7Z1Q_NIO)
options: (a) Include every deposited instance, as PoseBusters and the dataset README ("All instances of the ligand of interest") do, and disclose the four
(b) Restrict to pocket-equivalent copies (residue Jaccard >= 0.6), dropping the four alternates
(c) Include all but report a sensitivity row without them
decisions.recommendation: (a). It is the external convention and the decision is inert on the present data: no headline arm gains any complex from these four at d = 1, 15 or 30; 7TUO's alternate is a genuine second site 26 A away that no pose approaches within 17 A, and the other three are adjacent fragment copies 4.9-6.2 A from the reference with minimum alternate RMSD 2.1-2.6 A. A Jaccard threshold would add an arbitrary parameter for zero effect; one appendix sentence naming the four suffices.

decisions.question: Metal-adjacent stratum (78 of 303 within 5 A of a metal)
options: (a) Keep as a complex-level property defined on the reference copy, verify once that the alternates agree, register the (currently unregistered) generator
(b) Recompute per pose from the copy the pose is scored against
(c) Define as any copy within 5 A of a metal
decisions.recommendation: (a). The stratum is a receptor-preparation property of the complex, not of the pose; 139/143 alternates share the reference pocket so the count is expected to hold, and a one-off per-copy check confirms it. Only the stratum recovery rates (body_main_short.tex:868, body_appendix_short.tex:165) are recomputed. Register the computation in the harness because no script under Scripts/ produces the 78.

decisions.question: Crystal-cluster reach when several crystal sites exist
options: (a) Nearest crystal site: a cluster reaches if its centroid is within 4 A of ANY copy centroid; the crystal-closest cluster is defined by the nearest copy
(b) Reference site only (status quo)
(c) Count each crystal site separately (multi-site recovery, co-reach per site)
decisions.recommendation: (a). It is the cluster-level analogue of the per-pose rule, moves the pooled oracle to 99.7 % consistent with :476, and leaves the definitions of Figures 5/6 intact. Add a tie rule for the six ids whose adjacent copy sits 4.9-7.8 A from the reference and therefore inside the 8 A clustering radius (both copies may fall in one cluster; count once). Reject (c) as a new analysis the thesis does not need.

decisions.question: Column naming and backward compatibility in per_pose_metrics.csv
options: (a) Redefine rmsd, centroid_dist, bestfit_rmsd, contact_recovery, plif_recovery in place as nearest-copy; add *_ref twins, n_copies, nearest_copy_idx, nearest_copy_is_ref; write to a new report directory
(b) Keep rmsd as single-instance and add rmsd_nearest etc., switching every consumer script to the new names
(c) Two parallel CSVs, one per convention
decisions.recommendation: (a). Every consumer already reads rmsd as the gate, so redefining in place changes one producer instead of 14+ consumers; the *_ref twins preserve the old values for the sensitivity arm, and the new directory (e.g. pose_comparison_report_nearest or _v2) respects the never-overwrite rule and lets the harness diff old against new. pb_rmsd/pb_kabsch_rmsd/pb_rmsd_within_2A become nearest-copy automatically through the combined mol_true and need no rename.

decisions.question: Does the single-instance convention become the appendix sensitivity arm
options: (a) Yes: M2 Option B table with the columns inverted (nearest = primary, reference copy = sensitivity), plus the single-copy stratum row (Option D)
(b) No sensitivity arm, a one-sentence disclosure only
(c) Keep single-instance primary and add nearest-copy as the sensitivity arm (M2's original recommendation)
decisions.recommendation: (a). The plan has already chosen nearest-copy as primary; the reference-copy column then serves as the conservative bound the M2 note valued, and the single-copy stratum (165 complexes: 54.5/50.9/32.7 % rank-1) shows the ordering where no copy exists. Register it as one bitexact stage with yaml assertions (143/138 ids, gains 38/29/2 and 15/12/3).

decisions.question: How the Methods should describe the endpoint
options: (a) Redefine at body_main_short.tex:109-115 as RMSD to the nearest of all deposited copies chosen per pose by lowest in-place RMSD, that copy supplying every crystal reference for the pose, with the source benchmark's identical rule cited (README all instances, redock.yml load_all, check_rmsd minimum) and the single-instance value named as the sensitivity arm
(b) Leave :109 unchanged and describe the convention only in the appendix at :664
(c) Describe it as a correction for the blind box (a whole-protein-specific fix)
decisions.recommendation: (a). The endpoint definition belongs in the Methods, and the justification is external convention rather than box repair, so (c) would misstate it: the paper scored every method this way and its Vina anchor was inert only because the 25 A cube excluded the copies. Draft, house style: "Near-nativeness is the symmetry-corrected heavy-atom RMSD between a docked pose and the nearest of all crystallographic copies of the ligand deposited with the structure, computed in place without superposition. The copy with the lowest RMSD is chosen for each pose and supplies the centroid, form, contact and interaction references for that pose. This is the convention of the source benchmark, whose validity battery loads every deposited instance and reports the lowest RMSD. The 165 single-copy complexes are unaffected. The single-instance value is retained and reported as a sensitivity arm in Appendix ..."

decisions.question: Comparability with the PoseBusters paper's published Vina and DiffDock numbers
options: (a) State that the published values (Vina 58 % PB-valid, DiffDock 12 %, RMSD<=2: 59.7/38.0 % on the 308) were computed against the closest copy, so the switch aligns the scoring axis and only the search-space axis (25 A cube vs whole protein) still separates the studies; keep the :868 non-comparability sentence for the box axis
(b) Treat the published numbers as single-instance and keep the current text
(c) Quote no external numbers
